To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fyn is required for the expansion of T cells in vivo.

Fyn is essential for TCR mediated IL-2 production, which is necessary to support the expansion of T cells in vivo, and that the Fyn-Lck interaction regulates the threshold of IL-2 production required to promote T cell growth in vivo.
Fyn is required for TCR signaling, T cell proliferation, and T cell mediated disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how T cell signaling is regulated in the context of the immune response and how defects in these processes contribute to the onset of autoimmune disease.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate TCR signal transduction, and how these processes contribute to the development and progression of T cell dependent autoimmune diseases.
the mechanisms of T cell activation and T cell-mediated disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fyn is an indispensable regulator of T cell activation and function.
Fyn expression is required for both protective immunity and autoimmunity.
Fyn expression is required for both protective immunity and onset of autoimmunity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fyn and Lck are both required for the initiation and expansion of T cell responses.
the Fyn kinase has a dual function.
Fyn expression predicates both protective immunity and onset of autoimmunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Fyn/Lck signaling module is a central component of the T cell activation pathway, and that Fyn is a key determinant of the threshold for IL-2 production, which in turn is a key regulator of the T cell response.
the role of Fyn is to integrate and coordinate signals emanating from the TCR and co-receptors to regulate IL-2 production.
Fyn is not an essential component of the TCR signaling pathway, but rather a critical regulator of T cell function.
